newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt wins lower house confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt wins lower house confidence vote.

text.p: The Italian government on Wednesday won a lower house parliamentary vote of confidence on a decree law aimed at speeding up the approval process for starting or resuming state construction projects.
As expected, the centre-left government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi won the vote. The count was 310 for and 244 against.
The government called the confidence vote, the 23rd since taking office a year ago, to sweep away some 400 amendments that had been tabled by the separatist Northern League.
The construction decree, approved by the cabinet nearly two months ago, aims to streamline the approval process for starting or resuming public works projects that have been long frozen or stalled.
Many construction projects throughout Italy have been stalled for years since a corruption scandal exposed by graft-busting magistrates in Milan swept away Italy's old political order in 1992.
Many of the projects were exposed as lucrative sources of kickbacks and bribes from contractors.
